description: Combine the current n=1024+n=2048 global leader with the dependency-safe six-way 32-column n=256 graph. Import only the 384-CTA initial half-panel factor/solve path and matching LD36 sidecar stores while preserving all small, n=512, n=1024, n=2048, n=4096, and large-shape dispatches, then optimize cross-shape state and validate the full grid.

Merged both parent histories while preserving the first parent's complete n1024, n2048, small, n512, n4096, and large-shape dispatches. Imported only the second parent's six task-major initial n256 CTAs per matrix: each independently factors A00, solves one 32-column LD36 U01/U02/U03 half, and writes disjoint FP32 plus packed LD64 sidecar halves; task0 alone drains A00. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 benchmark cells passed. Aggregate measured 778.571 us under isolated tails. Batch64/n256 measured 82.756 us mean/66.314 best with one 3.211-ms sample versus second-parent 69.203/64.256. Preserved batch60/n1024 measured 933.148/890.816 us and batch8/n2048 2080.287/1499.600 us with one 109.894-ms sample, reproducing their clean floors near first-parent 890.880 and 1492.960 us.

Changed only the six-way n256 initial block mapping from task-major waves to sample-major groups, so each sample's six factor/half-panel CTAs are adjacent and can reuse the same A00 and panel cache lines while every other shape and graph node remains byte-identical. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Aggregate improved from tail-heavy Trial0 778.571 to 760.724 us. Batch64/n256 mean improved from 82.756 to 71.899 us as the worst sample fell from 3.211 ms to 0.919 ms, while clean best moved from 66.314 to 67.072 us. Preserved n1024 measured 913.304/890.720 us and n2048 1869.182/1505.984 us, with untouched paths returning near their parent floors.

Reordered the six initial n256 tasks into three 128-block panel waves, pairing each panel's two halves per sample to retain task-wide coverage while adjacent CTAs reuse A00/panel cache lines. Wrapped local import build and all 17 tests plus fresh-input guard passed, and benchmark cells0-2 completed, but exact batch64/n256 failed during remote Numba specialization: the new C integer named panel shadowed the existing panel pointer, causing four NVRTC errors in the linked loader/store source. No full-grid metric was emitted; the schedule requires a separate identifier-fix trial.

Fixed Trial2's remote C specialization by renaming the panel-group integer, preserving the three-wave paired-half schedule. The 384-block initial grid now launches 128 adjacent CTAs for both 32-column halves of each U01/U02/U03 panel before advancing, combining per-panel cache reuse with all-sample wave coverage. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and full 15-cell benchmark passed. Aggregate improved from sample-major Trial1 760.724 to 759.989 us. Batch64/n256 reached 69.294/66.284 us mean/best versus sample-major 71.899/67.072 and task-major Trial0 82.756/66.314, retaining the clean floor while reducing the largest tail. Preserved n1024 measured 910.803/890.912 us and n2048 1906.627/1506.464 us.

Applied a 96-register launch cap to the paired-wave n256 initial kernel, targeting the parent profile's 119-register initial node while preserving the exact six-way LD36 graph and every other dispatch. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch64/n256 measured 70.002/66.284 us mean/best versus uncapped Trial3 69.294/66.284: the clean floor was identical and the sampled mean rose 0.708 us. Aggregate measured 763.242 us versus Trial3 759.989, dominated by an unrelated 18.403-ms n1024 sample; n1024 clean best was 892.512 us and n2048 1504.384 us.

Tightened the paired-wave n256 initial launch cap from 96 to 80 registers as the second point of the profile-directed cap comparison, leaving the graph, traffic, and all other dispatches unchanged. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and full grid passed. Batch64/n256 measured 70.253/66.260 us mean/best versus cap96 Trial4 70.002/66.284 and uncapped Trial3 69.294/66.284; the clean floor moved 0.024 us while the mean remained within tail variation. Aggregate reached 758.754 us, the branch low, with n1024 938.246/892.800 us and n2048 1807.912/1491.216 us. The aggregate gain primarily reflects cleaner untouched cells rather than the register cap alone.

Acted on the exact Trial5 profile's no-spill 80-register initial kernel by removing the remaining four-column RHS pad: the six 32-column initial panels now use compact LD32 shared storage, reducing workspace from 26.62 to 25.62 KiB while retaining paired 128-CTA panel waves and every other dispatch. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch64/n256 improved from profiled LD36 Trial5 70.253/66.260 to 69.042/66.282 us mean/best; aggregate reached a branch-best 757.221 us versus 758.754. Preserved n1024 measured 904.765/888.800 us and n2048 1823.738/1500.512 us. Used the profile's 42-percent memory activity and duplicated A00 traffic to predicate the initial cp.async factor load to upper-triangular float4 segments only, leaving compact LD32 panels, the 384-CTA paired schedule, and all other paths unchanged. Wrapped build, all tests, guard, and full grid passed. Batch64/n256 measured 77.473/66.426 us mean/best versus full-tile Trial6 69.042/66.282, including a 2.211-ms tail; the clean floor rose 0.144 us, measuring the divergent triangular load as slower despite halving nominal factor bytes. Aggregate was 781.879 us under n256, n1024, and a 156-ms n2048 tail. Preserved clean n1024/n2048 bests were 896.992/1509.696 us.

Restored the full coalesced factor load, then changed task0's triangular A00 drain from two 16-lane float4 rows per warp to one full-warp float2 row, targeting the profile's 23.9-of-32-byte global-store sector utilization while retaining compact LD32 panels. Wrapped build, all tests, guard, and full grid passed. Batch64/n256 measured 71.080/66.304 us mean/best versus Trial6's original float4 drain 69.042/66.282; the clean floor was 0.022 us slower and the mean included a 0.972-ms tail. Aggregate measured 771.835 us under n512/n2048/large-shape drift; clean n1024/n2048 bests were 890.816/1501.856 us. The doubled drain instruction count did not move the target floor.

Restored Trial6's proven float4 factor drain, then removed the explicit post-TRSM CTA barrier before the LD32 panel/factor store to test whether MathDx's terminal synchronization already covered the handoff. Wrapped build and all 17 tests plus fresh-input guard passed, but exact batch64/n256 in the full grid produced NaN/Inf and the benchmark exited 112 with no metric. The solve/store handoff requires an explicit barrier; this invalid source is being reset before the next trial.

Split the initial factor/panel cp.async traffic into two groups. The kernel now waits only for A00, begins MathDx factorization while the LD32 half-panel remains in flight, then waits and synchronizes before TRSM; the explicit solve/store barrier and all other paths remain intact. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, guard, and full grid passed. Batch64/n256 clean best improved from Trial6 66.282 to 66.228 us, while a 3.943-ms tail inflated its mean to 85.729 us versus 69.042. Aggregate measured 785.301 us under that tail plus n512/n2048 drift, with clean n1024/n2048 bests 890.720/1494.272 us. The overlap moved the observed target floor by 0.054 us but needs a cleaner repeat to separate it from run noise.

Repeated Trial10's byte-identical two-group overlap source to separate its 66.228-us floor from the prior 3.943-ms target tail. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and full grid passed again. Batch64/n256 measured 69.362/66.174 us mean/best, improving Trial6's non-overlapped 69.042/66.282 clean floor by 0.108 us while returning to a normal sampled mean. Aggregate measured 758.308 us versus Trial6 757.221; n1024 reached 904.972/888.352 us and n2048 1887.428/1497.168 us. Across two exact overlap runs the target bests were 66.228 and 66.174 us, supporting the retained asynchronous panel/factor overlap despite unrelated aggregate variance.

Changed only the overlapped LD32 panel cp.async group from cache-all to cache-global, bypassing L1 for each unique half-panel while retaining cache-all for the six-times-reused A00 loads. Wrapped build, all tests, guard, and full grid passed. Aggregate reached 757.262 us, essentially matching Trial6's 757.221 branch best. Batch64/n256 measured 71.895/66.284 us versus cache-all overlap repeat 69.362/66.174, with a 1.180-ms tail and 0.110-us slower clean floor. n1024 and n2048 measured 908.953/892.960 and 1817.729/1499.744 us. L1 bypass did not improve the target floor, so cache-all remains the stronger overlap policy by clean evidence.

Completed the cache-policy comparison by restoring cache-all for unique panels and bypassing L1 only for the six-times-reused A00 factor loads. Wrapped build, tests, guard, and full grid passed. Batch64/n256 measured 74.143/66.282 us mean/best versus both-cache-all overlap repeat 69.362/66.174, including a 1.633-ms tail; its clean floor was 0.108 us slower. Aggregate measured 760.624 us, with n1024 905.340/890.656 and n2048 1840.669/1501.648 us. Both factor and panel groups therefore retain cache-all as the measured clean-floor winner among the three policies.

Restored cache-all for both overlap groups and replaced the linear 384-block index with a native (half=2, sample=64, panel=3) grid. The linked loader/store derive task state directly from blockIdx.xyz, removing linear panel/within-panel rematerialization while preserving identical paired scheduling. Wrapped build, tests, guard, and full grid passed. Batch64/n256 measured 72.262/66.286 us mean/best versus the linear-grid cache-all repeat 69.362/66.174, including a 1.226-ms tail; the clean floor rose 0.112 us. Aggregate measured 769.016 us under n512/n2048 drift. The linear paired grid retains stronger target evidence.

Restored the linear paired grid and both cache-all groups, then reordered task0's linked drain so A00 triangular output stores precede the solved panel/sidecar stores, testing whether releasing factor state first shortens the epilogue. Wrapped build, tests, guard, and full grid passed. Batch64/n256 measured 70.070/66.176 us versus panel-first overlap repeat 69.362/66.174: the clean floors differ by only 0.002 us and the mean by 0.708 us under normal tail variation. Aggregate measured 765.262 us under n1024/n2048 drift. The store order is target-neutral by measured floor.

Restored the selected panel-first, linear paired-grid, both-cache-all overlap source byte-identical to succeeded Trial11 after completing the drain-order and 3-D launch comparisons. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed.
